traps.shape: a host written as a fully qualified name with its root label on either the certificate name or the constraint, in every rfc822Name form and in the URI host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report shows one address form; a fix that canonicalises only that form, or only the certificate side, still matches the report

traps.shape: a subject distinguished name whose leading RDNs sit ahead of the permitted subtree's sequence
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory summary names mail and URI names only; the directory-name comparison is a separate algorithm in the same class and is not exercised by the reported example
traps.realistic_because: published fix site, bundled in the same commit but absent from the advisory summary

traps.shape: a mail address whose quoted local part itself contains the separator, so the host used for the comparison is not the address's host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about how the host is spelled, and an ordinary address contains exactly one separator; the published fix never touched this split and current upstream still splits at the first at sign
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code, still present in the latest upstream tree

traps.shape: a certificate that carries an excluded address in the subject distinguished name while its alternative-name extension also carries an allowed address
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported name is an alternative name, and the incoming code reads as a deliberate statement that the extension's addresses are the certificate's identities
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a plausible RFC 6125-style identity-precedence rule applied to a name-constraint check, in the path-processing layer the published fix never touches

traps.shape: one CA certificate that publishes permitted subtrees and excluded subtrees in the same extension, where the name is outside the permitted set but not excluded
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported CA publishes a single excluded subtree; a CA that publishes both kinds is a different configuration, and the incoming code reads as exclusion-wins precedence
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a misreading of the RFC 5280 precedence rule, in the constraint-ingestion layer the published fix never touches
